Composer: tabs [composer-tab-internal|external], 4 CTA cards [composer-cta-evidence_request|tracking_request|apology_refund|patience_carrier] each prefills [composer-body] (verified body length 181 chars after evidence_request click), [composer-send] POSTs and shows sonner toast. [detail-status-select] present; [detail-fullview] href=/admin/tickets/<id> ✓; [detail-take-btn] correctly HIDDEN since ticket is already assigned (count=0); [state-machine-claim-branch] correctly HIDDEN since no active_claim (count=0). 'back-to-bandeja' navigates back to /agente. State-machine bar shows Nuevo → En curso (current) → Esperando → Resuelto with status pill.

ui_bugs.issue: After '/' shortcut focuses [agent-filter-search], pressing 'Esc' does NOT blur the input. Consequently subsequent '?' press is captured by the search input (filters tickets) instead of opening the help modal. The shortcut handler intentionally skips when target is an input (correct UX), but Esc should also blur the focused input to restore the global shortcut context.

After reload, localStorage correctly restores 'cards' layout, but the layout button [data-testid='layout-cards'] has no aria-pressed/data-active attribute to indicate it is the current layout. Visual styling likely applied via Tailwind class but a11y/testability would benefit from aria-pressed='true'.

action_items: (Optional, low-prio) On Escape inside agent shortcut handler, also call document.activeElement?.blur() when target is the search input — so the next '?' press opens the help modal even after focusing search.
(Optional) Add aria-pressed='true' to the currently-selected layout button so the active state is testable/discoverable.

rca_of_the_issue: Minor frontend UX bug — KeyboardShortcutsHelp does not open when Esc is pressed after the search input was focused via '/'. Root cause: shortcuts.js useAgentShortcuts handler returns early when target.tagName is INPUT/TEXTAREA (which is correct to not hijack typing). However, on Escape the handler calls onClose but doesn't blur the input, so the next '?' keypress is captured by the still-focused input and ends up typed as text. Mitigation: extend the handler so that when key === 'Escape' AND editable, also do e.target.blur() before returning. This is a 2-line change in /app/frontend/src/pages/agent/shortcuts.js around L30-41. Verified by manual test: after explicit blur via page.evaluate, pressing '?' opens [data-testid='agent-shortcuts-help'] correctly.
